## Authoring model

Teaching repositories are treated as independent scholarly resources rather than folders copied into the personal website.

- An actual course, class, workshop, or training activity uses `type-training`.
- The reusable [`Scientific Training Template`](https://github.com/qselmer/.template-training) uses `type-template`.
- New lesson material should normally use Quarto (`.qmd`); Jupyter notebooks (`.ipynb`), R scripts, Python code, and other executable formats remain appropriate when they serve the learning objective.
- A teaching repository may publish its own Quarto site under `qselmer.github.io/<repository>/`.
- This website provides discovery, classification, and stable navigation only.

## Inclusion policy

A repository is promoted to this catalogue only when it has a defensible teaching identity: a defined learning purpose or sequence, sufficient documentation, explicit provenance and attribution, and a canonical public source.

Practice repositories, clones, copied tutorials, and partially adapted external material are not presented as authored teaching activities until their pedagogical structure and provenance are clear. The website-level selection is recorded in `teaching/registry.json`; the canonical repository inventory remains in the academic-profile repository.
